annotations.text:
Wireframe v1: layout and structure only.
Visual design (colors, fonts, icons) comes after this structure is approved. The only colors used so far are the 7 level colors (green, blue, purple, yellow, orange, red, black).
Step names and per-level counts come from the source syllabus. Videos, counts, suggested BPM and loop times are placeholders.
Example step: Maxie Ford (Level 1).

1. Step list
- Top: search (names + aliases) and Filter button
- 1 to 7: jump straight to a level
- Each level collapses/expands; only Level 1 is open at first
- Essential steps first, optional steps listed separately below
- The metronome bar stays pinned to the bottom of every screen

2. Filters (bottom sheet)
- Level and category: pick any number
- Essential / Optional: pick one of three
- The button shows how many steps match

3. Step detail (scrolls)
- Video sits right under the title so you can practice right away
- Speed, loop and mirror controls under the video
- Description, then breakdown and count, tips, learn-first and next steps
- Bottom: previous / next step within the level

4. Practice mode
- Opens from 'Practice mode' on the detail screen
- The A–B loop is marked on the timeline (shaded)
- Big buttons so they're easy to hit mid-practice
- Mirror flips the video like a mirror

5. Metronome
- Tap the bottom bar to expand; keeps ticking when collapsed
- BPM: slider, ±5, tap tempo (tap along and it works out the BPM)
- Suggested tempos per step (slow / normal)
- Works while a video is playing

6. Desktop
- Left: list (search, filters, levels). Right: selected step
- Clicking a step only changes the right side, so flipping through steps is quick
- The metronome sits fully expanded along the bottom right
